--- title: "Stochastic delay differential equations" course-unit: a02-stochastic-delay-differential-equations status: complete --- ## Why this unit matters - The DDE of the previous unit is still **deterministic**: same history in, same trajectory out, every time. - Real epidemics have finite populations and demographic noise, exactly like the chemical-Langevin SDE. - This unit combines both — a diffusion approximation **and** a fixed recovery delay — using the current, maintained `DelayDiffEq` + `StochasticDiffEq` route (not the archived `StochasticDelayDiffEq.jl`). - The official docs mark `SDDEProblem` **experimental** — this deck shows, concretely, what that means. ::: {.notes} Set expectations up front: this is the one unit in the course whose headline result is "here is where the software combination currently breaks, and here is the documented workaround." That is itself the pedagogical point. ::: ## Model assumptions and classification Same population, contact process, and fixed delay $\tau = 1/\gamma = 4$ as the DDE unit. Transmission and recovery now carry chemical-Langevin noise, applied to the *delayed* recovery flow. | Property | Classification | |---|---| | Determinism | Stochastic | | Time / state | Continuous / continuous (diffusion approx.) | | Noise | Chemical Langevin, non-diagonal, history-dependent | Not guaranteed to stay inside $S, I, R \ge 0$ — the central caveat below. ## Equations $$ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{d}S &= -\lambda(t) S\, \mathrm{d}t - \sqrt{\lambda(t) S}\, \mathrm{d}W_1, \\ \mathrm{d}I &= \bigl[\lambda(t) S - \lambda(t-\tau) S_{t-\tau}\bigr]\mathrm{d}t + \sqrt{\lambda(t) S}\, \mathrm{d}W_1 - \sqrt{\lambda(t-\tau) S_{t-\tau}}\, \mathrm{d}W_2, \\ \mathrm{d}R &= \lambda(t-\tau) S_{t-\tau}\, \mathrm{d}t + \sqrt{\lambda(t-\tau) S_{t-\tau}}\, \mathrm{d}W_2 \end{aligned} $$ Noise columns cancel across compartments by construction, so $S+I+R$ stays conserved for *any* realized path — nonnegativity is a separate question. ## Julia API ```julia using DelayDiffEq, StochasticDiffEq prob = SDDEProblem(sir_dde!, sir_delayed_noise!, u0, history, tspan, p; noise_rate_prototype = noise_shape()) Random.seed!(4) # NOT the rng= keyword — see caveats sol = solve(prob, LambaEM(); dt = 0.1, adaptive = false) ``` `DelayDiffEq` now recognizes an `SDDEProblem` directly and wraps `LambaEM` in `MethodOfSteps`, exactly as it wraps `Tsit5` for the deterministic DDE. ## Adaptive stepping breaks down ::: {#cell-code-slide-a02-adaptive .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code} using DelayDiffEq, OrdinaryDiffEq, StochasticDiffEq, SparseArrays, Random function sir_dde!(du, u, h, p, t) S, I, R = u; β, c, τ = p; N = S + I + R λ = β * c * I / N Sd, Id, Rd = h(p, t - τ); Nd = Sd + Id + Rd λd = β * c * Id / Nd du[1] = -λ * S; du[2] = λ * S - λd * Sd; du[3] = λd * Sd return nothing end function sir_delayed_noise!(G, u, h, p, t) S, I, R = u; β, c, τ = p; N = S + I + R infection = max(β * c * I / N * S, 0.0) Sd, Id, Rd = h(p, t - τ); Nd = Sd + Id + Rd recovery = max(β * c * Id / Nd * Sd, 0.0) G[1,1] = -sqrt(infection); G[2,1] = sqrt(infection) G[2,2] = -sqrt(recovery); G[3,2] = sqrt(recovery) return nothing end sir_history(p, t) = [1000.0, 0.0, 0.0] u0 = [990.0, 10.0, 0.0]; p = (0.05, 10.0, 4.0); tspan = (0.0, 40.0) noise_shape() = sparse([1.0 0.0; 1.0 1.0; 0.0 1.0]) Random.seed!(4) prob_probe = SDDEProblem(sir_dde!, sir_delayed_noise!, u0, sir_history, tspan, p; noise_rate_prototype = noise_shape()) sol_probe = solve(prob_probe, LambaEM()) (sol_probe.retcode, round(sol_probe.t[end]; sigdigits = 3), length(sol_probe.t)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ::: {.ansi-escaped-output} ```{=html}

Contrast explicitly with the non-delayed chemical-Langevin SDE chapter, where a per-step clamp is at least a *local* fix — here it is not, because the delayed recovery term reaches back into history that a current clamp cannot touch. ::: ## Interpretation and limitations 1. **Adaptive stepping is currently unusable** at the history discontinuity; a fixed step sidesteps it but forfeits automatic error control. 2. **The `rng` keyword is unreliable** for this `SDDEProblem` / `MethodOfSteps` combination — reproducibility currently requires global `Random.seed!` before `solve`, unlike every other stochastic unit in this course. 3. **Nonnegativity is not guaranteed**, and harder to police than for a plain SDE because the delayed term cannot be corrected by clamping the present state alone. None of this invalidates the chemical Langevin approximation itself — it remains best treated as a teaching device and basis for further testing with the *current* package versions, not a production tool. ## Key takeaways - `SDDEProblem` unifies delayed drift with chemical-Langevin diffusion, but is explicitly experimental in current SciML docs. - Use a **fixed step** (`adaptive = false`) and a **global** `Random.seed!` — both deliberate, documented deviations from the rest of the course. - Conservation holds structurally; nonnegativity does not — always check the minimum state, not just the sum. - A discrete-event alternative (next unit) avoids the diffusion approximation and its negative-state risk entirely. ## Further reading - [SDDE problem reference](https://docs.sciml.ai/DiffEqDocs/stable/types/sdde_types/) (marked experimental) - Gillespie (1977) for the chemical Langevin approximation - Full derivation, code, and exercises: [book chapter](../../appendices/02-stochastic-delay-differential-equations.html)
